advances: Intrinsic geometry within a single input parity. It does not impose parallelism across all sampled fibers.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: The trace is a finite disjoint union of compact convex fibers, so its Hausdorff dimension is the maximum of their affine dimensions. A fiber of positive input mass must have dimension $q$. For any cross pair of such fibers, $p$ is integer by the parity hypothesis and $(C_z+C_w)/2\subseteq C_p$ by convexity. The direction of the affine hull of a Minkowski sum is the sum of the two directions. Therefore the two $q$-dimensional directions agree, since $\dim C_p\le q$. A fixed positive input fiber on each side compares all input fibers. The midpoint body has dimension $q$ with affine hull $(b_z+b_w)/2+L$, and its inclusion in $C_p$ forces this to be the affine hull of $C_p$.
statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty mixed trace $S$ and $q=\dim_H S>0$. In one base parity class let two finite nonnegative measures have positive mass and be absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal H^q|_S$. All input fibers of positive mass on either side have one common $q$-dimensional direction $L$. For any product pair of these input bases $z,w$, the midpoint base $p=(z+w)/2$ is sampled and the actual fiber $C_p$ has dimension $q$ and direction $L$. Writing each input affine hull as $b_z+L$ with $b_z\in L^\perp$, the perpendicular offset of $C_p$ is $(b_z+b_w)/2$ and depends only on $p$ within that class.
title: Common fiber directions within one midpoint parity
